newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman, Turkish official meet on grain ban.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman, Turkish official meet on grain ban.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman and Turkish Ambassador Nuzhet Kandemir met Friday to discuss Turkey's recent imposition of strict grain import standards, and the officials said afterwards they were hopeful a current stalemate between the countries can be resolved soon.
"I am hopeful that we can work through these matters ... I got a positive impression," Glickman told reporters.
"We may be thinking about modifying the rules" to fit with U.S. and global import standards, said Kandemir.
The officials were apparently unaware of reports released from Turkey while they were meeting that Turkey has decided to ease its ergot fungus limit for imported grains to 0.05 percent.

USDA stopped issuing export certificates for wheat shipments to Turkey two weeks ago when Turkey began imposing a zero tolerance level on ergot. Turkey this week said it would ease its tolerance level to 0.02 percent, but USDA officials and exporters have said that is still too low.
Glickman said the recently imposed strict tolerances are "impossible to meet not only by us but by anybody."

But even if Turkey agrees to raise its ergot tolerance level to 0.05 percent, problems still remain, as Turkey has also announced it would begin imposing zero tolerance levels on a variety of other diseases that impact most of the grains and oilseeds that the United States exports to Turkey.
The USDA notified inspectors at U.S. ports Wednesday evening to stop issuing phytosanitary certificates for all shipments of grains and oilseeds to Turkey until the problem is resolved.
Kandemir said he would pass on the U.S. concerns to his government. Officials said no time frame was agreed to, but that they hoped the issue would be settled soon.
Glickman said he stressed to the Turkish official that the current regulations negatively impact not only U.S. shipments, but shipments from all other countries.
